Back:
security of tenure
- cannot be dismissed arbitrarily
- salaries cannot be tampered with by the executive or legislature
- cannot be removed except on grounds of infirmity, incapacity or gross misconduct

Division: Original

original jurisdiction: hears cases beying jurisdiction of state courts (e.g. damages more than 250k)
supervisory jurisdiction: ensures all inferior courts and tribunals act within their jurisdiction
revisionary jurisdiction: power to call for and examine proceedings of the state courts for correctness and legality of decisions

deck: 5 The Courts & Adjudication & 6 Legal Profession & Professional Training
Back:
1997 Asian Financial crisis halted econ growth
Govt decided to liberalise key sectors like finance, local law community needed cross-border technical and legal expertise
- Foreign firms allowed to practise permitted areas of SG law

● In
1999, Legal Services Review Committee (LSRC) set up to review liberalisation of Singapore’s legal
sector

○ Recommended encouraging top global law
firms to open offshore offices, and for MNCs to relocate their in-house counsel
in SG

■ Increase talent pool of FLs and thus the
legal knowledge base within SG, and also potentially increase amount of
cross-border legal work attracted to SG

○ Recommended awarding scholarships and
grants to local legal talent to study aboard and acquire expertise in
cross-border transactions, which was not available in SG itself

○ Recommended AGAINST full liberalisation

■ Fears of “cherry-picking” of local lawyers
by foreign firms, and overwhelming competition from foreign law practices

■ Recommended partial liberalisation through Joint Law Ventures (JLV) and Foreign Law
Alliance (FLA) schemes

From 2000
to 2004, few JLVs and FLAs were set
up, and they quickly dissolved
